Switched probes
===============

Import Probes.module's Switched theory and write:

  (probe STATS (++ trimmed))
  (probe STATS (call stats_add COUNTER trimmed))

A probe is a statement. Its switch must be a constant expression; a variable
switch is refused. When the switch is nonzero the effect runs as written.
When it is zero the effect is not evaluated and emits no code, yet the
compiler still checks it: undeclared names, wrong argument types and
invalid operations are errors in every build. A counter that only probes
read is used by those probes, so it is not reported as set but unused.

The effect is inserted as written in the caller's scope. A probe adds no
names and introduces no return, break, continue or goto.

Cost
----

With the switch off, optimized code equals the program written without the
probes and their counters. Unoptimized code still initializes probe-only
locals; only their updates and the probe effects disappear. State that only
probes read, such as record fields, still occupies memory and still receives
stores outside probes. Keep its declaration under the same switch with
ordinary C conditionals, and update it only inside probes.

A no-op macro that discards its argument hides the argument from the
compiler. The disabled build then neither checks the probe nor sees its
counters used.

Native tests cover both switch states at O0 and O2, effects and their
counts, sink references only when enabled, removal of disabled probes,
checking of disabled probes, a variable-switch refusal, native export and
identical objects against handwritten C.
